standard_prerequisites.use: Etale morphisms of algebraic spaces and surjective etale charts, geometric points and their liftings, strict henselisation of a local ring, and the definition of flatness for a module on an algebraic space. The comparison of the three conditions is retained.

core_obligations: Show that a chart U, V, W with a, b, c etale and a point u over x always exists, and reduce the comparison of the three conditions to a common such chart together with a geometric point lifting along U -> X.

Use the strict henselisation identifications O_{X,x} = O_{U,u}^{sh} and the corresponding ones for Y and Z to prove the chain of equivalences that identifies flatness of F at x over Y with flatness of F_w at u over V_w.

proof_roadmap.step: Note that condition (2) is independent of the chosen K-rational point and construct a chart U, V, W as in (3) by successive surjective etale choices.

spans.label: independence of the point and existence of the chart

proof_roadmap.step: Choose a geometric point of U lifting the given one of X, identify the strict henselisations of X, Y, Z with those of U, V, W at the chosen points, and rewrite the flatness condition in those terms.
Close the chain of equivalences showing that flatness of F at x over Y holds exactly when F_w is flat at u over V_w.

difficulty_reason: The lemma establishes the equivalence of three descriptions of flatness of F on the fibres of X -> Z over a point x: one through a geometric point and the fibre of the local ring, one through a K-rational point and the fibre product, and one through an etale chart U, V, W with a point u. The proof first shows that a chart as in (3) always exists by successive surjective etale choices, then passes to a common refinement using a geometric point lifting along the etale map U -> X, identifies the strict henselisations O_{X,x} = O_{U,u}^{sh} and likewise for Y and Z, and finally chases a chain of equivalences relating flatness of F at x over Y to flatness of the pulled-back sheaf on the fibre over w. The non-routine content is the transport of the flatness condition across the strict henselisation identifications and the final chain of equivalences, not any single step. Retained author proof at lines 5665-5787.
